builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Shifter Quantization: Compact Representations for Native Integer Computation
summary: Shifter Quantization replaces standard groupwise weight quantization by reconstructing native-width integer operands via shared appended and shifted bits, enabling standard INT MMA to span the full dot product, with an SHI variant using INT4 kernels. It requires adopting a new weight format and its associated custom kernels rather than using off-the-shelf llama.cpp or vLLM quantization paths. Adoption can fail if the released kernels lack support for the reader's models, GPU architecture, or serving framework, or if the reported throughput gains do not reproduce on different hardware and workloads.
rationale: The method targets exactly the single-GPU local inference setting and claims simultaneous speed and quality gains over llama.cpp and vLLM baselines, but the gains depend on custom SQ/SHI kernel implementations whose availability and maturity must be verified before adoption.

claims.statement: Shifter Quantization replaces standard groupwise weight quantization by reconstructing native-width integer operands via shared appended and shifted bits, enabling standard INT MMA to span the full dot product, with an SHI variant using INT4 kernels. It requires adopting a new weight format and its associated custom kernels rather than using off-the-shelf llama.cpp or vLLM quantization paths. Adoption can fail if the released kernels lack support for the reader's models, GPU architecture, or serving framework, or if the reported throughput gains do not reproduce on different hardware and workloads.

SQ2/SHI2 achieve 2.71-3.77x the 4,096-token prefill throughput of llama.cpp on a Q2_K checkpoint with 6.6-7.8% lower WikiText-2 KL; SQ4 achieves 1.43-2.47x prefill throughput over NInfer groupwise baselines with 24-40% lower KL; SQ8 achieves 27.4% higher batch-one prefill throughput and 72.7% lower KL than vLLM's online FP8.
